conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Bullet Time
style.description: A frozen moment: in a bright white high-speed-photography studio a striped orange ball bounces in and drops into a big white bowl of cobalt-blue liquid, and mid-splash TIME STOPS — the crown, its beaded rim, the spray of droplets and the ripples hang perfectly still while the camera keeps sweeping a near-full circle around them. Two clocks: timewarp.js maps video time t to WORLD time w(t) (run, freeze, reverse, forward, release, with linear rate ramps, so w is piecewise quadratic and exact), and separately lays out the camera arc. Every world thing — the ball's bounce and plunge, the lathe-profile crown with pinching lobes, ballistic droplets, floor splats, the cavity, ripples and the rebound jet — is a closed-form function of w, never stepped, so time can be scrubbed backward (the splash un-happens) and forward again. Sound follows w: every bounce, impact, pinch and droplet landing is cued wherever w(t) crosses it (reversed re-crossings included), with jog ticks while scrubbing and a pitch-dropping whir into the freeze. A two-track overlay gauge (CAMERA vs WORLD) shows the decoupling.
motion: Two clocks: video time t drives the camera; world time w(t) = integral of a piecewise-linear rate (run 1, freeze 0, reverse < 0, forward, release) drives everything else.
Every world object is a closed-form function of w (ballistic droplets, beta-bump crown and jet profiles, travelling ripples): seekable, reversible, never stepped.
The camera never stops: one long Catmull-Rom arc (azimuth, radius, elevation, target) sampled into dense keys; the world freezes inside it.
Sound follows w: each world event is cued wherever w(t) crosses it, forward or reversed; jog ticks every fixed step of w while scrubbing; a gliding whir on every rate ramp.

notes.mechanism: timewarp.js: world rate dw/dt is piecewise linear in video time (run 1, freeze 0, reverse -0.36, forward 0.36, release 1, crawl 0.05), so w(t) is piecewise quadratic; ball, crown, droplets, splats, cavity, ripples and jet are closed-form functions of w; the camera follows a separate Catmull-Rom arc.
